 JUDGEMENT
Heard finally, with the consent of the parties.

2] This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 08.04.2019, passed by I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandleshwar (M.P.) in Claim Case No.73/2018 whereby, a compensation of Rs.1,54,080/- has been awarded to the appellant.

entities.text: I Additional Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mandleshwar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
3] In brief, the facts of the case are that the appellant Kali Bai met with an accident on 18.11.2017 when she was going along with her husband Gal Singh by road from Dharampuri to Khalghat, at that time, the motorcycle bearing registration No.MP-12-BA-7817 being driven by respondent No.1 rashly and negligently, dashed against the appellant, as a result of which, her left leg suffered three fractures and on her entire body also, she suffered various bruises, and to claim the compensation in respect of the aforesaid injuries suffered by Kali Bai, a claim case was filed before the Claims Tribunal, who, after recording the evidence has passed the aforesaid award to the tune of Rs.1,54,080/-, and being aggrieved of the inadequacy of the same, the present appeal has been filed.
4] Counsel for the appellant has submitted that the income of the appellant has been considered by the Claims tribunal to be Rs.4,500/- only, which should have been Rs.9,000/-, and only 12%
disability has been considered, which should have been 48% as per the statement of PW-2 Dr.
Dinesh Thakur.
It is also submitted that under other heads also meager amount has been awarded.
Thus, it is submitted that the award may be enhanced appropriately.
5] Counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company, on the other hand, has opposed the prayer.

6] Having considered rival submissions and on perusal of the record, it is found that the injured has indeed suffered a comminuted compound fracture of tibia and fibula, for which she was also hospitalized for a period of fifteen days from 23.11.2017 to 01.12.2017.

Regarding her income, the Claims Tribunal has observed that since she has not proved her income, considering the fact that she was a daily wager, her income has been taken to be Rs.4,500/- per month, however, this Court is of the considered view that her income ought to have been considered to be at least Rs.5,500/- per month instead of Rs.4,500/-, and under other heads also, some amount needs to be enhanced.
In view of the same, the calculation can be made in the following manner, vis-a-vis the calculation made by the Claims Tribunal:-

The calculation made by the claims Tribunal:-
 Dependency 4500 X 12 X 7 X 12% 45,360  Medical expenses 78,720

The calculation made by this Court is as under :-
Permanent Disability 5,500 X 12 =66,000 73,920 66000 X 16% (PD) =10560 X 7
Medical expenses 78,720 Attendant charges 10,000
Special diet 10,000 Pain and suffering 20,000 Loss of wages for 3 months 16,500 Total 2,09,140

Amount awarded by the Tribunal - 1,54,080 Amount to be enhanced 55,060 7] In view of the above,
the appeal stands partly allowed and the appellant shall be entitled to receive an additional enhanced amount of Rs.55,000/- (in round figure) towards the compensation along with the interest as awarded by the Tribunal.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Bahar Kali Bai vs Virendra on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65937399/
